parse.name: .env.example
parse.src:
# Copy this file to ".env" and fill in your Kite Connect credentials.
# Get these from the Kite developer console: https://developers.kite.trade/apps

KITE_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
KITE_API_SECRET=your_api_secret_here

# Port this backend listens on.
PORT=3001

# IST dates that ARE trading sessions despite falling on a weekend — NSE's muhurat
# and other special sessions. Comma-separated ISO dates, e.g.
#   EXTRA_SESSION_DAYS=2026-11-08,2027-10-29
# Without this, intraday capture skips them (the gate is weekday-based) and their
# buckets can only ever come from the Kite historical backfill.
#
# The reverse case — a weekday that is an exchange HOLIDAY — needs no configuration:
# capture asks the exchange's own timestamp whether anything traded today and skips
# the day by itself, so the charts don't gain a flat session that never happened.
EXTRA_SESSION_DAYS=

# Where the frontend runs (used for CORS + post-login redirect).
# NOTE: Use 127.0.0.1 (not localhost) so it matches the Kite Redirect URL.
FRONTEND_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5173

# IMPORTANT: In the Kite developer console, set your app's
# "Redirect URL" to your frontend verify route. Kite requires HTTPS, but
# allows a http://127.0.0.1 URL for local testing (localhost is NOT allowed
# unless you serve the frontend over HTTPS). Use exactly:
#   http://127.0.0.1:5173/zerodha/verify
# and browse your app at http://127.0.0.1:5173 (not http://localhost:5173).

# Full-admin secret - required for /admin/verify (Zerodha login + trades + all).
ADMIN_SECRET=your_secret_key_here

# Trade-access password - required for /admin/access (view & take trades only,
# NO Zerodha login controls). Shares the same trades as the full admin.
ACCESS_SECRET=your_trade_access_password_here

# Shared secret for GET /api/internal/kite-token. The local "market_data"
# recorder calls this endpoint (header: x-internal-secret) to reuse THIS app's
# Zerodha access token, so it needs no separate Kite subscription. Use a long
# random string and set the SAME value as INTERNAL_TOKEN_SECRET in market_data.
# If left blank, the endpoint is disabled (returns 503).
INTERNAL_TOKEN_SECRET=

# Passcode for the public, curl-friendly token route:
#   GET /api/kite/token?passcode=...   (or header x-token-passcode)
# Once the admin has connected Zerodha, anyone with this passcode can fetch the
# day's access token via a simple curl (no admin login needed). Keep it separate
# from ADMIN_SECRET so it can be shared with scripts without granting admin
# access. Use a long random string, e.g. `openssl rand -hex 32`.
#
# ONE passcode covers BOTH brokers' token routes and the rf read:
#   GET /api/kite/token   -> { authenticated, api_key, access_token, login_date }
#   GET /api/dhan/token   -> { authenticated, client_id, access_token, expires_at,
#                              login_date }
#   GET /api/rf           -> { rf }
#
#   curl "https://<host>/api/dhan/token?passcode=YOUR_PASSCODE"
#   curl -H "x-token-passcode: YOUR_PASSCODE" https://<host>/api/dhan/token
#
# Each token route answers 409 when that broker has no live (unexpired) session, rather
# than serving a dead token.
#
# BECAUSE IT IS SHARED, THE TWO BROKERS ARE NOT INDEPENDENTLY REVOCABLE: rotating this
# rotates access to both, and a leak exposes both. That is the accepted tradeoff for
# managing a single secret.
#
# Keep it separate from ADMIN_SECRET — an admin token can place, close and delete trades
# and switch broker, whereas this grants only a token read.
#
# TREAT WHAT THESE ROUTES RETURN AS A TRADING CREDENTIAL. A Dhan access token plus the
# client id can place and cancel orders. Your DHAN_STATIC_PUBLIC_IP whitelisting bounds
# that to the whitelisted IP, so do NOT whitelist a host you only meant to give read
# access to.
#
# If left blank every route above is DISABLED (503). An unset secret NEVER means
# "no passcode required".
TOKEN_ROUTE_SECRET=

# MongoDB connection string (Mongoose) for persisting calendar-spread trades.
# Include the database name in the URI itself, e.g.
#   mongodb+srv://user:pass@cluster.mongodb.net/calspread?retryWrites=true&w=majority
# If left blank, the trades feature is disabled (the rest of the app still works).
MONGODB_URI=

# MongoDB connection string for the trade/charges LEDGER (collection: trade_log).
#
# Every trade writes one append-only document per event (entry, exit) recording
# what was transacted and what it cost: the contract value, the per-leg fills,
# and the full charge breakdown (brokerage, STT, exchange transaction charge,
# SEBI turnover charge, GST, stamp duty) exactly as Zerodha's virtual contract
# note API returned it — including the raw API payload, so the record survives a
# future change to Zerodha's charge heads. Exit documents also carry gross P&L,
# total charges and net P&L for the round trip.
#
# It is separate from MONGODB_URI because the ledger is accounting data: the
# `trades` documents are mutable (updated on close, deletable from the UI),
# whereas these are never rewritten, so the tax record of a trade outlives the
# trade itself and the collection can be exported for book-keeping as-is.
# Include the database name in the URI, e.g.
#   mongodb+srv://user:pass@cluster.mongodb.net/calspread_ledger?retryWrites=true&w=majority
# If left blank, the ledger is written to the MONGODB_URI database instead.
TRADE_LOG_URI=

# MongoDB connection string for the nse_fno ARCHIVE database (read-only).
# Contains historical stock_futures data up to Aug 31, 2025 (fnodata1 cluster).
# Example: mongodb+srv://user:pass@fnodata1.mongodb.net/nse_fno?retryWrites=true&w=majority
# If left blank, historical spread computation for pre-2026 dates is disabled.
NSE_FNO_ARCHIVE_URI=

# MongoDB connection string for the nse_fno CURRENT database (read-write).
# Contains stock_futures data from Jan 1, 2026 onwards (fnodata2 cluster).
# This is where new daily F&O closing data is written by the EOD scheduler.
# Example: mongodb+srv://user:pass@fnodata2.mongodb.net/nse_fno?retryWrites=true&w=majority
# If left blank, EOD stock_futures capture is disabled.
NSE_FNO_CURRENT_URI=

# MongoDB connection string for the spread database (read-write).
# Contains spread_daily and spread_summary collections (calspread cluster).
# Example: mongodb+srv://user:pass@calspread.mongodb.net/calspread?retryWrites=true&w=majority
# If left blank, spread computation and summary are disabled.
NSE_FNO_SPREAD_URI=


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Upstash Redis (REST) — durable store for the Analytics caches.
#
# Copy both values from the Upstash console: your database -> Connect -> REST.
# They look like:
#   UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL=https://your-db-name-12345.upstash.io
#   UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN=AX...long-token...
#
# What this buys you. Without it the option/futures OI frames, the per-minute
# chain snapshots behind the OI Δ% / buildup windows, and the previous-session
# close baseline all live only in memory — so every deploy or crash throws the
# session away and rebuilds it with hundreds of Kite historical calls, and any
# multi-day history (2 days, 1 week) is lost until it is re-accumulated. With it
# set, the backend warm-loads all of that on boot and only asks Kite for the gap.
#
# Retention is enforced in Redis (pruned buckets are deleted and every key
# carries a TTL), so nothing needs cleaning up by hand:
#   option/futures OI frames   1m -> 1 day, 5m -> 3 days, 15m -> 7 days, 1h -> 7 days
#   per-minute chain snapshots 1 day     (serves the 1m/5m/15m/1h windows)
#   per-hour  chain snapshots  4 days
#   previous-session close     2 days
#
# Cost: one pipelined request per minute during market hours, about 10-12 commands
# in it (~4K/day, ~90K/month). That fits the Upstash free tier's 500K/month with
# plenty of room. Key TTLs are refreshed at most every 15 minutes rather than on
# every write, which is what keeps the count down.
#
# If left blank the app behaves exactly as it did before Redis existed:
# everything stays in memory and is rebuilt from Kite after a restart.
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL=
UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN=

# Fair Value: full-admin, read-only option valuations; independent of trading.
# Default off. A saved full-admin analytics setting may override this default.
FAIR_VALUE_ENABLED=false
# Hard deployment disable: saved/UI analytics settings cannot override true.
FAIR_VALUE_DISABLED=false
# Optional validated JSON settings patch. Supply a verified expiry-time policy
# and discount curve/explicit flat fallback. See docs/FAIR_VALUE.md for all settings.
FAIR_VALUE_CONFIG_JSON=



# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Box arbitrage (PAPER BY DEFAULT; LIVE ONLY WHEN DOUBLE-GATED)
#
# An independent module (src/box/) that reuses this app's Kite session, shared
# WebSocket, instrument cache and Zerodha charge estimator. Three modes simulate
# fills; live mode can place broker orders only when BOTH deployment gates below
# are explicit, Mongo/Kite/reconciliation are healthy, and full-admin runtime
# controls are armed. See README section 7 and src/box/LIVE_EXECUTION.md.
#
# Box positions use their own collections (box_trades, box_trade_events) in the
# MONGODB_URI database, so the calendar trade book is untouched. With no
# MONGODB_URI the box scanner refuses to start rather than operating unrecorded.
#
# EVERY VALUE BELOW IS OPTIONAL — the defaults are the shipped specification and
# keep execution in paper_latency with live trading disabled.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Dedicated MongoDB connection string for the BOX collections (box_trades and
# box_trade_events), so the Box strategy book can live in its own database,
# entirely apart from the calendar trade book. Include the database name in
# the URI, e.g.
#   mongodb+srv://user:pass@cluster.mongodb.net/calspread_box?retryWrites=true
# If left blank, the box collections are created in the MONGODB_URI database
# instead (still their own collections, so calendar data is never touched).
# With BOTH this and MONGODB_URI unset the box scanner refuses to start rather
# than operating without durable records.
BOX_MONGODB_URI=

# THE ENTRY GATE: minimum GROSS edge (₹) from the SPREAD alone.
#
#   grossEdge = ((K2 - K1) - executableBoxCostPerUnit) x lotSize
#
# Charges are still estimated, stored and displayed — they are simply NOT
# deducted before deciding to enter, because fees are managed by hand.
MIN_BOX_GROSS_EDGE=1200

# OPTIONAL additional floor (₹) on the projected NET edge
# (gross - entryFees - estExitFees - safetyBuffer).
# 0 (the default) disables it, so the gross spread above is the only gate. Set a
# positive number to also require an after-cost cushion.
MIN_BOX_NET_EDGE=0

# Whether to skip a box whose charges Zerodha could not price. This is NOT about
# the threshold (which is gross-only): the exit rules are evaluated net of
# charges, so a position with no charge figures could never have its net P&L
# computed and would never auto-exit. Set to false to enter anyway and manage
# those positions by hand.
BOX_REQUIRE_PRICED_CHARGES=true

# Conservative slippage/safety allowance (₹) per complete box round trip, on top
# of the real Zerodha charges. Reported in the projected NET edge (and used by the
# optional net floor above), but NOT part of the gross entry gate.
BOX_SAFETY_BUFFER=150

# How long (ms) an UNCHANGED order book is still trusted.
#
# This is NOT a "price age" limit. A depth feed only sends a message when the book
# CHANGES, so silence is not staleness: a resting book nobody has touched for ten
# seconds is still the current, executable book. Illiquid F&O strikes are quiet for
# long stretches, so a sub-second value here does not make the system safer — it
# simply makes it unable to trade anything but the most active names.
# All four legs must pass, and the check is re-applied after the charge call.
BOX_QUOTE_MAX_AGE_MS=15000

# FEED LIVENESS (ms): maximum age of the newest tick across the WHOLE universe.
#
# This is the check that actually catches "we are holding old data and do not know
# it" — a silently dropped WebSocket leaves every cached book looking normal. With
# hundreds of instruments subscribed something is always trading during market
# hours, so universal silence means the connection is broken rather than the market
# being calm. When it trips, no entry and no automatic exit happens at all.
BOX_FEED_MAX_AGE_MS=5000

# Maximum age (ms) of the underlying value used to place the ATM window.
BOX_UNDERLYING_MAX_AGE_MS=10000

# A deliberate LOWER bound (₹) on what a round trip can cost in charges, used
# ONLY by the prefilter and ONLY when MIN_BOX_NET_EDGE above is turned on. It must
# UNDER-state real charges: a larger value would discard boxes that would have
# qualified. Eight option orders at ₹20 brokerage plus GST is already about ₹189,
# so 160 is safe.
BOX_PREFILTER_CHARGE_ALLOWANCE=160

# ATM re-centring damps. The spot must move past the midpoint between the current
# ATM and its neighbour by this extra fraction of a strike step before the seven-
# strike window moves, and a window is never rebuilt more often than the interval.
BOX_ATM_HYSTERESIS=0.15
BOX_WINDOW_MIN_INTERVAL_MS=15000

# Automatic-exit rules. A box closes when EITHER
#   remainingEdge <= max(FLOOR, PCT x entryNetEdge) AND currentNetPnL >= MIN_EXIT_NET_PNL
#   OR currentNetPnL >= PROFIT_CAPTURE_PCT x entryNetEdge
# and in both cases only while the net P&L is positive and all four reversed legs
# have fresh one-lot touch liquidity.
BOX_CONVERGENCE_FLOOR=200
BOX_CONVERGENCE_PCT=0.2
BOX_MIN_EXIT_NET_PNL=600
BOX_PROFIT_CAPTURE_PCT=0.75

# Minutes before the 15:30 IST close, on expiry day, to start forcing an
# executable close so a position is never abandoned at expiry. If the touch
# cannot fill it, the condition is recorded and exposed - never faked.
BOX_EXPIRY_SAFETY_MINUTES=45

# Cadences (ms): open-position monitoring, the slow flush of live figures to
# Mongo, the SSE publish rate to the UI, and universe/expiry/window refresh.
BOX_MONITOR_INTERVAL_MS=1000
BOX_PERSIST_INTERVAL_MS=30000
BOX_PUBLISH_INTERVAL_MS=500
BOX_UNIVERSE_REFRESH_MS=60000

# How often (ms) the LAST-CLOSE view is rebuilt while the market is shut. Pressing
# RUN outside market hours never trades: it shows each box priced from the last
# traded / closing prices so a mispricing at the close is still visible, marked
# price_source "last_close" and status INDICATIVE. Costs one REST /quote call per
# 500 instruments, and the numbers cannot move while the exchange is closed.
BOX_INDICATIVE_REFRESH_MS=60000

# Cap on simultaneously subscribed box option tokens. Zerodha allows roughly
# 3,000 instruments per WebSocket connection and the calendar board already uses
# part of that budget on the SAME shared socket, so this bounds the box universe.
# Underlyings that do not fit are reported in skipped_symbols on /api/box/status.
# Legs of an OPEN position are always subscribed regardless of this budget.
BOX_MAX_SUBSCRIBED_TOKENS=2200

# Optional hard cap on how many underlyings are scanned (0 = no cap beyond the
# token budget above).
BOX_MAX_UNDERLYINGS=0

# Charge-estimate cache TTL (ms) and how many charge calls may be in flight.
BOX_CHARGE_CACHE_TTL_MS=30000
BOX_CHARGE_CONCURRENCY=3

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Local charge rate card (units matter — read the suffix on each line)
#
# These are the statutory/broker rates the local calculator bills. They are the
# largest cost in a box round trip, so a wrong value here silently makes every
# paper P&L wrong. Verify against zerodha.com/charges for YOUR account.
#
# STT: PERCENT of premium, sell side only. 0.15% since 1 April 2026, when option
# STT was flattened to a uniform rate (futures went 0.02% -> 0.05% at the same
# time). The previous default here was 0.10%, which understated the biggest cost
# in the trade and flattered results.
BOX_STT_SELL_PCT=0.15
# Round the STT head to the NEAREST RUPEE, as the contract note does.
BOX_STT_ROUND_NEAREST_RUPEE=true
# NSE options transaction charge: PERCENT of premium, both sides.
BOX_EXCHANGE_TXN_PCT=0.03503
# NSE IPFT: RUPEES PER CRORE of premium (not a percent). Rs 50/crore on options.
BOX_IPFT_PER_CRORE=50
# SEBI turnover fee: PERCENT of premium, both sides (Rs 10 per crore).
BOX_SEBI_PCT=0.0001
# Stamp duty: PERCENT of premium, BUY side only.
BOX_STAMP_DUTY_BUY_PCT=0.003
# GST: PERCENT applied to (brokerage + exchange txn + SEBI).
BOX_GST_PCT=18
# Flat brokerage per executed option order (RUPEES).
BOX_BROKERAGE_PER_ORDER=20
#
# Identifier for the rate card above, stamped onto every trade and execution
# attempt. Statutory rates change, so a P&L figure is only interpretable next to
# the rates that produced it. Bump this whenever you change a rate.
BOX_CHARGE_RATE_VERSION=zerodha-nse-options-2026-04-01

# Which Box execution model is used. FOUR values are accepted:
#
#   paper_touch     fill at the touch visible in the DETECTION snapshot (optimistic)
#   paper_latency   (default) fill from the latest valid book at a simulated arrival
#   paper_legging   FOUR independent simulated orders with emergency unwind
#   live            broker-authoritative execution; blocked unless the separate
#                   BOX_LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED gate is also true
#
# Unknown values fail closed during configuration. The default remains paper_latency
# so existing deployments cannot start placing real orders after an upgrade.
BOX_EXECUTION_MODE=paper_latency
# Independent deployment kill switch. Setting this alone does nothing; live requires
# BOTH BOX_EXECUTION_MODE=live and BOX_LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true.
BOX_LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=false

# Live runtime controls still start false on every process start and must be armed
# through the full-admin API. See src/box/LIVE_EXECUTION.md before enabling live.
BOX_LIVE_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS=60000
BOX_LIVE_FEED_RECONNECT_WARMUP_MS=5000
BOX_LIVE_MAX_OPEN_BOXES=1
BOX_LIVE_MAX_CONCURRENT_EXECUTIONS=1
BOX_LIVE_MAX_RESIDUAL_LEGS=1
BOX_LIVE_DAILY_LOSS_LIMIT=5000
BOX_LIVE_REJECT_LIMIT=3
BOX_LIVE_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURE_LIMIT=3
BOX_LIVE_MAX_OPEN_LEG_QUANTITY=100
BOX_LIVE_MAX_GROSS_OPEN_LEG_QUANTITY=400
BOX_LIVE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS=5000
BOX_LIVE_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS=3000
BOX_LIVE_WORKING_TIMEOUT_MS=30000
BOX_LIVE_PARTIAL_TIMEOUT_MS=10000
BOX_LIVE_CANCEL_TIMEOUT_MS=5000
BOX_LIVE_MAX_MODIFICATIONS=2
BOX_LIVE_MAX_CHASE_TICKS=2

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# TRANSPORT PACING — real broker rate limits, NOT simulated latency.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# These two are REAL waits. They exist because the broker enforces a request rate,
# and lowering them below the documented floors earns a 429 (which, at Zerodha,
# still consumes the daily order-request budget). They are NOT the paper simulation
# delays: BOX_SIMULATED_DECISION_MS and BOX_SIMULATED_LATENCY_MS are paper-only and
# are never consulted on the live path.
#
# GENERAL pacing: order-status polls, order/position lists, funds, margins, health.
# Also the poll cadence while waiting for a working order to resolve. Unchanged.
BOX_LIVE_BROKER_MIN_INTERVAL_MS=250
#
# ORDER-MUTATION pacing: place / modify / cancel only. 0 = derive from the broker's
# published order limit (Zerodha 110 ms, floor 100 ms from its documented 10 order
# requests/second; Dhan 120 ms, matching the floor its own HTTP layer imposes).
# A positive value is an operator override and is CLAMPED UP to the broker floor —
# this is a real rate limit, so it can be relaxed towards the floor but never below
# it and never to zero. Cancellation is in this faster bucket deliberately: a
# protective cancel is the operation you least want to slow down.
BOX_LIVE_BROKER_ORDER_MIN_INTERVAL_MS=0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FOUR-LEG ENTRY BURST
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# How many ENTRY role submissions of ONE Box may be in transport at once (1..4).
#
# A live concurrency slot is held for an order's ENTIRE lifecycle, submit through
# terminal polling. With BOX_LIVE_MAX_CONCURRENT_EXECUTIONS=1 leg 2 is not even
# persisted until leg 1 fully resolves, so the Box sits UNHEDGED for three complete
# order lifecycles. This bounds how many of the four may be in flight together.
#
# ENTRY only, and scoped to a single Box pipeline, so it can never let two
# overlapping candidates bypass contract reservations. Burst slots are invisible to
# emergency/cancel/exit admission, so an entry burst cannot delay protective work.
# Broker rate limits are still enforced independently by the pacer above.
#
# 1 = exactly the pre-existing serialised behaviour. 4 = recommended for production.
BOX_LIVE_ENTRY_SUBMIT_CONCURRENCY=1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MAXIMUM ₹ PER BOX  (an admission metric — NOT broker margin)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Refuses an entry whose four bounded LIMIT orders would transact more than this
# many rupees. 0 = disabled (the default, so existing deployments are unaffected).
#
# THE NUMBER IS:  gross_entry_order_notional_rupees
#                 = SUM( |limit_price x quantity| ) over the four ENTRY legs,
#                   computed from the ACTUAL immutable bounded LIMIT requests.
#
# IT IS **NOT** BROKER MARGIN, and must never be described as such. A four-leg Box
# is a hedged structure: its real margin requirement is typically a small fraction
# of gross option notional, and can even be a net CREDIT. An operator who read
# "margin" here and set a matching cap would be off by roughly an order of
# magnitude. If a broker margin estimate is available it is reported separately as
# broker_estimated_margin_rupees and is never substituted for this metric.
#
# Checked from the immutable order requests BEFORE any broker submission, and
# re-verified at dequeue (the last safe moment). Exactly at the cap is admitted;
# one paisa over is refused. Exits are never gated by it.
BOX_LIVE_MAX_BOX_CAPITAL_RUPEES=0
# Paper mirror, for exercising the same admission arithmetic under live_parity.
# LIVE remains the authoritative safety gate. 0 = disabled.
BOX_PAPER_MAX_BOX_CAPITAL_RUPEES=0

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ONE ACTIVE BOX PER UNDERLYING  (optional strategy restriction)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# When true, a second Box may not enter on an underlying that already has one,
# REGARDLESS of strike pair, expiry or direction: RELIANCE 2500/2600 active blocks
# RELIANCE 2550/2650 even though they share no option contract.
#
# WHY: concurrent same-underlying Boxes can hold opposite option roles that
# economically offset each other, so the broker's net position per contract no
# longer decomposes cleanly per Box — which makes reconciliation, partial-exit
# accounting and residual attribution much harder exactly when they matter most.
#
# This is an ADDITIONAL layer. It never replaces the existing exact-contract
# reservations, and with it false the behaviour is unchanged. Refusals are reported
# as `underlying_already_active`, never as a contract-reservation conflict.
#
# ENTRY only: it can never block an exit, a protective cancel or a residual flatten.
BOX_ONE_ACTIVE_BOX_PER_UNDERLYING=false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SESSION CYCLE BUDGET  (one-shot trading)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# How many COMPLETE Box lifecycles an armed session may run.
#   0 = unlimited (default)
#   1 = one-shot
#   N = N cycles
#
# A "complete lifecycle" is ENTRY -> HOLD/MONITOR -> EXIT -> FLAT. It is NOT "one
# broker order", and reaching the limit does NOT stop the engine: monitoring,
# auto-exit, partial-exit cleanup, residual flattening, reconciliation and recovery
# all continue. Only NEW ENTRY is disabled.
#
# A cycle is CONSUMED when a full four-leg Box is established (which is what gates
# new entry, so with max=1 the second candidate is refused while the first Box is
# still open) and COMPLETED when that Box reaches fully FLAT. A rejected,
# partially-filled-then-unwound or economics-aborted entry establishes no Box and
# therefore consumes nothing.
#
# The counters are DURABLE (collection `box_trading_session`). Restarting Node does
# not hand back a spent budget, and if the record cannot be READ, entry fails CLOSED
# — an unread session is not an unarmed one. A session must be armed explicitly
# through the full-admin API; arming is refused while any consumed cycle still has
# live exposure, so it cannot be used to bypass the limit.
BOX_SESSION_MAX_COMPLETED_TRADES=0

# paper_legging leg submission: "parallel" (default, all four at once) or
# "sequential" (each next order only after the previous FILLED).
BOX_LEG_EXECUTION_MODE=parallel
# How long (ms) a leg may rest before it is deemed unfilled and the box aborts.
BOX_LEG_TIMEOUT_MS=500
# Simulated latency (ms) for the emergency unwind of a partial/aborted fill.
BOX_LEG_UNWIND_LATENCY_MS=150

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DEDICATED BOX MARKET-DATA LANE
#
# Two physically separate upstream WebSockets for the ONE active broker:
#
#   futures lane — calendar-spread board, spot, futures analytics, browser SSE
#   box lane     — option strikes for the Box scanner (bid/ask/depth)
#
# This is NOT two brokers at once. Exactly one broker is ACTIVE and both lanes
# belong to it: two Zerodha sockets, or two Dhan sockets, never one of each.
#
# Why: sharing one connection makes the two workloads compete for one token
# budget, and every strike the board displaces is an arbitrage the scanner cannot
# see. Split, each lane has its own refcount table, its own budget and its own
# health — so a wide option universe cannot starve the board and vice versa.
#
# Connection budget. Zerodha permits 3 sockets per API key: two are used here
# (one per lane) and the third is deliberately left free for a separate service.
# PM2 stops the old process before starting the new one, so a deploy never needs
# four. Dhan permits 5 sockets per user at 5000 instruments each, so two lanes fit
# comfortably. The lane count is fixed at two by construction — no code path opens
# an unbounded number of sockets.
#
# Turning this off falls back to the single shared feed, exactly as before.
BOX_DEDICATED_MARKET_FEED=true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SHARED-CONTRACT EXECUTION COORDINATION
#
# Two Box opportunities can need the SAME option contract. A 1300/1320 box and a
# 1320/1340 box have different candidate keys (underlying|expiry|K1|K2|DIRECTION)
# and both trade the 1320 strike. Every duplicate guard in the engine is keyed on
# that candidate key, so without this layer the two look unrelated and can be
# submitted in the same instant — each assuming the whole displayed size at 1320.
#
# The coordinator wraps the execution gateway, so it sits ABOVE the paper/live
# branch: paper is coordinated by exactly the same code as live. A simulator that
# lets two boxes consume one resting lot is not modelling anything real.
#
# Unrelated boxes are NOT serialised: two boxes sharing no contract execute
# concurrently, and there is no global execution mutex.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Master switch. Turning this off restores the un-coordinated behaviour in which
# overlapping boxes can submit the same contract simultaneously. Emergency escape
# hatch, not a tuning knob.
BOX_EXECUTION_COORDINATOR_ENABLED=true
# How long (ms) a box may wait for a contract another execution holds. This is the
# GIVE-UP bound, not the normal path: the loser is woken by the holder's release,
# typically within a millisecond, then RE-PRICED before it may proceed. Raising it
# only keeps dead opportunities alive longer.
BOX_CONFLICT_WAIT_MAX_MS=250
# Reservation TTL (ms). The crash-recovery mechanism — a dead or wedged execution
# cannot hold a contract past it — and also how long a reservation is HELD when the
# terminal broker state was ambiguous, so keep it well above a round trip.
BOX_INSTRUMENT_LOCK_TTL_MS=5000
# Optional per-underlying execution budget; 0 disables it. A risk cap layered ON TOP
# of exact-contract exclusion, never a replacement — RELIANCE 2500CE and RELIANCE
# 2800CE share no contract and must still be able to execute concurrently.
BOX_MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_UNDERLYING=2
# Fraction of the originally detected gross edge that must survive for a box that
# waited on a conflict to be allowed to execute. Arriving at the front of the queue
# is not a reason to trade.
BOX_CONFLICT_REVALIDATE_MIN_EDGE_RATIO=0.8
# Require a DURABLE (cross-process) reservation tier before LIVE execution runs.
# Off by default because this deploys as a single PM2 fork process, where the
# in-process store is authoritative and strictly stronger than a network lock: it
# cannot time out, fail or be delayed. Set true when running multiple workers —
# live execution then fails CLOSED instead of silently losing conflict protection.
BOX_RESERVATION_REQUIRE_DURABLE=false
# Build the DURABLE (cross-process) reservation tier. ON by default: the in-process
# store is only authoritative for ONE process, and the moment there are two — PM2
# cluster mode, several workers, another EC2 instance, a Kubernetes replica — both see
# the same option contract as free and both submit. MongoDB is already mandatory for
# the Box module, so this adds no new operational dependency.
# When it cannot be reached: LIVE Box ENTRY fails closed; exits, residual flattening
# and reconciliation stay available; paper degrades to a labelled local_only mode.
BOX_DURABLE_RESERVATIONS_ENABLED=true
# How often a held reservation is renewed. Defaults to a third of the lock TTL, so two
# consecutive renewals may fail before the lease is genuinely at risk. A bounded timer,
# NOT one renewal per market tick — that would be thousands of writes a minute.
BOX_RESERVATION_RENEW_INTERVAL_MS=1666
# Clock-skew grace for durable expiry decisions. Creates an asymmetric dead band: the
# holder stops claiming ownership this long BEFORE its lease expires, and a challenger
# may only reclaim it this long AFTER. Handing a contract to nobody for 2x this is a
# missed opportunity; handing it to two workers is a naked position.
BOX_RESERVATION_CLOCK_SKEW_GRACE_MS=250
# How long a reservation held over an UNRESOLVED broker state keeps being renewed.
# Unbounded renewal would lock a strike all day on one ambiguous outcome; no renewal
# would drop protection while real exposure may still exist. After this it is left to
# lapse by TTL — never actively released, because releasing is the "assume there is no
# exposure" mistake. Residual flattening is not gated by any of this.
BOX_RESERVATION_UNCERTAIN_HOLD_MAX_MS=60000
# Lock NAMESPACE. Development, staging and production MUST NOT share one, or a laptop
# pointed at the production cluster could take a contract the real trading process
# needs — or believe it holds one production is actively trading.
#
# LEFT UNSET DELIBERATELY. A copied .env carrying a hard-coded value is exactly how two
# environments end up in one namespace, so set it explicitly per deployment, e.g.
#   CALSPREAD_DEPLOYMENT_ID=production-mumbai
# Unset, it falls back to NODE_ENV and then "development" — so production and a laptop
# are still separated as long as NODE_ENV is set. Starting LIVE without an explicit
# value logs a warning.
CALSPREAD_DEPLOYMENT_ID=
# Optional host/replica label used in owner ids and conflict logs. Defaults to the
# machine hostname; PM2's NODE_APP_INSTANCE is folded in automatically when set.
CALSPREAD_INSTANCE_ID=
# Net two boxes wanting OPPOSITE sides of one contract against each other.
# MUST stay false until the ledger can represent virtual ownership of both boxes
# while broker net exposure is zero. Until then opposite-side overlaps take the same
# safe path as same-side ones: serialise, confirm, re-evaluate.
BOX_INTERNAL_NETTING_ENABLED=false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# paper_legging: EXECUTABLE ORDER PRICING (marketable-limit, not a market order)
#
# A simulated leg no longer consumes whatever the book shows on arrival. Each
# order carries a LIMIT a bounded number of ticks past the touch it was priced
# against, and the book is walked only down to that limit — a level worse than the
# limit is never filled. This is the difference between "pay up to ₹100.10" and
# "pay whatever is showing".
#
#   BUY  limit = reference_ask + chaseTicks × tickSize
#   SELL limit = reference_bid − chaseTicks × tickSize
#
# Entries chase a small band; emergency unwinds may reach wider because flattening
# exposure matters more than the price. The real instrument tick size is used
# where the dump supplies it; BOX_DEFAULT_TICK_SIZE is the fallback.
BOX_LEG_MAX_CHASE_TICKS=2
BOX_UNWIND_MAX_CHASE_TICKS=5
BOX_DEFAULT_TICK_SIZE=0.05

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# paper_legging: CONSERVATIVE QUEUE APPROXIMATION
#
# We cannot see NSE order-level queue priority from level-2 depth, so we do NOT
# pretend the displayed quantity is all ours.
#
#   BOX_QUEUE_MODEL=haircut (default) treats only a fraction of each displayed
#     level as executable for us: effectiveQty = floor(displayed × (1 − pct/100)).
#   BOX_QUEUE_MODEL=none uses the raw displayed quantity — the optimistic baseline
#     to compare against.
#
# Deterministic (no randomness): the same recorded book + same config always fills
# identically. This is a transparent approximation, NOT a reconstruction of true
# queue position — see README §7.
BOX_QUEUE_MODEL=haircut
BOX_QUEUE_LIQUIDITY_HAIRCUT_PCT=30

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# paper_legging: FOUR-LEG TEMPORAL COHERENCE
#
# Maximum spread (ms) between the newest and oldest leg EXCHANGE timestamps a
# candidate may show and still auto-enter. When all four legs carry a valid
# exchange timestamp and the dispersion exceeds this, the candidate is rejected as
# "cross_leg_time_skew" rather than traded on books that are not a coherent
# cross-sectional snapshot. 0 disables the check. When any leg lacks an exchange
# timestamp the check is skipped and the existing receive-time freshness logic
# stands (a missing timestamp is never itself grounds for rejection).
BOX_MAX_CROSS_LEG_EXCHANGE_DISPERSION_MS=250

# Asynchronous verification of the LOCAL charge maths against Zerodha's virtual
# contract note. Never blocks execution — a trade is already open by the time this
# runs. Retries are BOUNDED so a broker outage cannot become a hot retry loop, and
# per-head differences (brokerage / STT / exchange / SEBI / GST / stamp) are stored
# on the trade so a drifted statutory rate can be identified rather than guessed at.
BOX_CHARGE_RECONCILE_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3
BOX_CHARGE_RECONCILE_RETRY_BASE_MS=5000

# How many opportunities the UI is sent.
BOX_MAX_PUBLISHED_OPPORTUNITIES=60

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Box daily P&L cache + nightly archive (OPTIONAL, OFF by default)
#
# When enabled AND Upstash Redis is configured (UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL/TOKEN
# above), the RUNNING net P&L of the day's box trades — open positions plus every
# trade closed today — is mirrored to Redis on a slow cadence. This is a fast,
# restart-surviving cache of "how is today going", NOT a replacement for the
# box_trades book (entries/exits still persist to Mongo exactly as before).
#
# Once a night a cron drains that day's cached P&L into a dedicated MongoDB
# collection, `box_daily_pnl` (one document per trade per day, plus a per-day
# summary). The drain is STREAMED — one document at a time with a small delay —
# so a day's rows are never written in a single burst, and a failure part-way
# through is retried on the next pass rather than losing data. Two later passes
# re-check the day and finish anything the first drain missed.
#
# With BOX_PNL_CACHE_ENABLED unset/false, none of this runs: no Redis writes, no
# new collection, and the module behaves exactly as it did before.
BOX_PNL_CACHE_ENABLED=false

# How often (ms) the running day-P&L snapshot is written to Redis while enabled.
# One small pipelined request per interval, so 30s is inexpensive.
BOX_PNL_CACHE_INTERVAL_MS=30000

# TTL (seconds) on a day's cached P&L hash in Redis. Must comfortably outlive the
# verify passes below (default 3 days) so a delayed/retried archive still has the
# cache to read from.
BOX_PNL_CACHE_TTL_SEC=259200

# IST hour (0-23) at which the day's cached P&L is drained to Mongo. Default 21
# (9 PM), well after the 15:30 close so the day is final.
BOX_PNL_ARCHIVE_HOUR=21

# IST hours (comma-separated, 0-23) at which the archive is re-checked and
# completed if the 9 PM drain did not finish. Default "22,23" (10 PM & 11 PM).
BOX_PNL_VERIFY_HOURS=22,23

# Delay (ms) between each document while streaming the archive into Mongo, so the
# nightly transfer never lands as one bulk write. Default 50ms.
BOX_PNL_ARCHIVE_DRAIN_DELAY_MS=50


# ============================================================================
#  DHAN (DhanHQ v2) — the SECOND broker
#
#  Calspread supports two brokers: Zerodha and Dhan. Historical trades from both
#  coexist in the database forever, but ONLY ONE broker is ever active for market
#  data, the Box scanner, the quote/depth feed, new trades, live order execution,
#  positions, reconciliation, margins and charges.
#
#  Leaving this whole block unset is fine: the app boots Zerodha-only exactly as
#  before and reports Dhan as "not configured".
#
#  Create the API key/secret at web.dhan.co → My Profile → "Access DhanHQ APIs" →
#  toggle to "API key". Keys are valid for 12 months.
# ============================================================================

# Your Dhan client id (the numeric account id shown in the Dhan dashboard).
DHAN_CLIENT_ID=

# The API key and secret of your Dhan app.
#
# THE SECRET IS SERVER-SIDE ONLY. It is sent to Dhan as a request header from this
# process and is never returned by any endpoint or exposed to the browser.
DHAN_API_KEY=
DHAN_API_SECRET=

# Where Dhan sends the browser after a successful login. This MUST match the
# redirect URL configured on the Dhan app EXACTLY, or the login fails.
#
# The frontend serves this path and forwards the ?tokenId=... to the backend, which
# exchanges it for an access token. The token never reaches the browser.
DHAN_REDIRECT_URL=https://calspread.online/dhan/verify

# Dhan's order-update postback endpoint. Optional but recommended.
#
# Treated strictly as a HINT that accelerates order-state updates — REST
# reconciliation remains the source of truth, because a postback can be lost,
# duplicated, reordered or arrive unauthenticated.
DHAN_POSTBACK_URL=https://calspread.online/api/dhan/postback

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Dhan safety gates. Both default to the SAFE setting.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Master switch for REAL Dhan orders. With this false, Dhan can serve market data
# and paper trading but the live execution adapter refuses to be constructed.
DHAN_LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=false

# Whether Dhan's data APIs may be used at all. Default true.
DHAN_DATA_ENABLED=true

# STATIC IP — read this before enabling live Dhan trading.
#
# Dhan requires the CALLER'S PUBLIC IP to be whitelisted before it will accept order
# placement, modification or cancellation.
#
# PREFERRED: set the server's public IP here. Dhan exposes its own whitelist via
# GET /ip/getIP, so this value is VERIFIED against Dhan's primaryIP/secondaryIP
# rather than trusted. That turns the precondition from a declaration into a checked
# fact, and readiness then reports exactly which side disagrees.
#
# Verified at boot (when Dhan is active) and on every switch to Dhan. After
# whitelisting a new address, POST /api/dhan/verify-ip re-checks it without a restart.
DHAN_STATIC_PUBLIC_IP=

# Manual declaration, retained as an ADDITIONAL operator gate.
#
#   - With DHAN_STATIC_PUBLIC_IP set: the API check decides readiness. This flag is
#     then only a kill switch — setting it explicitly false still blocks trading even
#     when the IP verifies.
#   - With DHAN_STATIC_PUBLIC_IP unset: this flag alone decides, and the health report
#     says so, because a declaration is materially weaker evidence.
#
# Defaults to FALSE and FAILS CLOSED throughout. Note that setting it true without
# actually whitelisting the IP does not make orders work — it only removes the local
# guard, and Dhan then rejects the orders at the edge, potentially part-way through
# building a four-leg box.
DHAN_STATIC_IP_EXPECTED=false

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Dhan transport tuning (optional)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Per-request deadline (ms). `fetch` has no timeout of its own, so this is what
# stops an unresponsive socket from wedging the request pacer.
DHAN_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS=8000

# Minimum gap between Dhan API requests (ms) — a simple, predictable pacer that
# keeps us clear of Dhan's per-endpoint rate limits.
DHAN_MIN_INTERVAL_MS=120

# Attempts for a RETRYABLE READ, including the first. Order submissions are NEVER
# retried regardless of this value.
DHAN_MAX_READ_ATTEMPTS=3

# Depth levels to subscribe: 5 (default), 20 or 200.
#
# Leave at 5. The Box scanner watches thousands of strikes and the FULL packet's
# 5-level ladder is what it is sized for. Dhan's 20- and 200-level feeds are a
# separate architecture with far tighter instrument limits (200-depth is one
# instrument per connection), so forcing the scanner onto them would exhaust
# connections rather than improve a decision.
DHAN_DEPTH_LEVEL=5

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Dhan charges — NOT the same as Zerodha's
#
#  The statutory heads (STT, exchange transaction charge, SEBI fee, stamp duty,
#  GST) are set by the exchange and government and are identical at every broker.
#  BROKERAGE is not. A four-leg box round trip is EIGHT orders, so a per-order
#  difference is multiplied eightfold against a ₹1,200 entry gate — which is why
#  Dhan trades are costed with Dhan's card and labelled `dhan_estimate`, never
#  with Zerodha's.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Flat brokerage per executed order (₹). Set this to match YOUR Dhan plan.
DHAN_BROKERAGE_PER_ORDER=20

# Statutory rates. Change only when the government does.
DHAN_STT_SELL_PCT=0.1
DHAN_EXCHANGE_TXN_PCT=0.03503
DHAN_IPFT_PER_CRORE=50
DHAN_SEBI_PCT=0.0001
DHAN_STAMP_DUTY_BUY_PCT=0.003
DHAN_GST_PCT=18

# Stamped onto every Dhan trade so a historical record stays interpretable after a
# rate change.
DHAN_CHARGE_RATE_VERSION=dhan-nse-options-2026-04-01


# ===========================================================================
# LIVE-CALIBRATED EXECUTION TWIN
#
# Everything in this block is ADDITIVE and defaults to today's behaviour.
# Nothing here enables live trading, and nothing here changes the default
# execution mode. See src/box/LIVE_EXECUTION.md for the full model, the
# calibration honesty contract, and the "Observable parity" section stating
# exactly what the simulator can and cannot claim.
# ===========================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PAPER EXECUTION PROFILE
#
#   standard     Today's paper behaviour, byte-for-byte. The default.
#   live_parity  EVIDENCE-DRIVEN. Shared-liquidity ledger, the live scheduling
#                policy, latency drawn from MEASURED live samples when
#                calibration is valid, and a real cancel-vs-fill race window.
#                Nothing in this profile is fabricated.
#   stress       RESILIENCE TESTING ONLY. Deliberately injects faults (broker
#                slowdown, feed gaps, rejects, duplicate/out-of-order events).
#                A SEPARATE profile precisely so an injected fault can never be
#                mistaken for measured behaviour.
#
# `stress` is never a fallback: an unrecognised value becomes `standard`, and
# STARTUP REFUSES if `stress` is combined with BOX_EXECUTION_MODE=live.
BOX_PAPER_EXECUTION_PROFILE=standard

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LIVE-CALIBRATION CONSUMPTION (live_parity only)
#
# How much measured evidence paper requires before it trusts a distribution.
# Below these thresholds it falls back to the documented constants and reports
# `measured: no` / `confidence: LOW` — it never presents a constant as a
# measurement.

# Fresh measured samples before a calibrated distribution is used at all.
BOX_PAPER_CALIBRATION_MIN_SAMPLES=30

# Fresh samples before a TIME-OF-DAY bucket (OPEN / NORMAL / CLOSE) is trusted
# on its own rather than pooled. Deliberately higher than the value above:
# activating a narrow bucket on a handful of observations is the definition of
# overfitting, and produces confident-looking numbers with no basis.
BOX_PAPER_CALIBRATION_BUCKET_MIN_SAMPLES=60

# Samples from sessions older than this are excluded from ACTIVE calibration.
# They are still RETAINED for analytics and drift detection — the point is that
# yesterday's latency regime must not silently calibrate today. 3 days: long
# enough to survive a weekend gap, short enough that a fortnight-old network
# regime never applies.
BOX_PAPER_CALIBRATION_MAX_AGE_MS=259200000

# Enable coarse OPEN / NORMAL / CLOSE bucketing at all. Buckets still have to
# earn their own sample count above before being used.
BOX_PAPER_CALIBRATION_TIME_BUCKETS=true

# Fallback cancel-request -> terminal window (ms) for paper's cancel-vs-fill
# race, used when no measured CANCEL latency exists yet.
#
# DELIBERATELY NON-ZERO. Zero would mean "cancels are instantaneous", which is
# the optimistic assumption the race model exists to remove: in reality the
# exchange can still fill a resting order while our cancel is in flight.
BOX_PAPER_CANCEL_LATENCY_MS=150

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# EXECUTION TIMING OBSERVABILITY
#
# Records monotonic stage timestamps for every real broker operation — queue
# wait, transport pacing, HTTP, broker ACK, each cumulative fill, cancel
# request/confirmation — and feeds them to the calibration store paper reads
# from. This is the mechanism by which the simulator becomes more accurate as
# real executions are observed.
#
# FAIL-OPEN AND OFF THE HOT PATH: it performs no I/O, never awaits, and every
# method is individually guarded, because it runs inside protective-cancel and
# unwind paths. Lost measurement is counted and reported, never hidden.
BOX_EXECUTION_TIMING_METRICS_ENABLED=true
BOX_EXECUTION_TIMING_WINDOW=500

# Measure event-loop delay and process pressure.
#
# WHY IT MATTERS: "POST->ACK took 900ms" has two very different explanations —
# the broker was slow, or the broker replied in 90ms and our event loop was
# blocked for 810ms. Only one of those belongs in a broker latency
# distribution, and a sample measured during a significant stall is therefore
# EXCLUDED from calibration. Cheap (native histogram, one low-frequency timer)
# and fail-open.
BOX_EXECUTION_EVENT_LOOP_METRICS_ENABLED=true

# Deployment region LABEL for calibration data. Never auto-detected, and a
# calibration store REFUSES to import another region's samples: two deployments
# have different physical round-trip times to the broker, so a merged
# distribution would describe neither.
# BOX_DEPLOYMENT_REGION=ap-south-1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CALIBRATION PERSISTENCE
#
# Without this, a restart at 09:30 throws away the morning's evidence and drops
# paper back to its constants — exactly when calibration is most valuable.
#
# Bounded and asynchronous by construction: recording is one in-memory append
# with no await and no I/O. A full buffer drops the OLDEST observations and
# reports the loss; a failed flush discards the batch rather than growing memory
# without bound. Losing latency samples is survivable; losing the trading
# process is not. No substitute samples are ever generated.
BOX_LIVE_TIMING_PERSIST_ENABLED=false
BOX_LIVE_TIMING_BATCH_SIZE=50
BOX_LIVE_TIMING_FLUSH_MS=15000

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SHADOW VALIDATION MODE
#
# The REAL market feed and the REAL strategy run, paper live_parity produces the
# orders it would have produced, and NO BROKER ORDER IS EVER SUBMITTED. This
# gives a continuous, zero-risk stream of predictions to compare against real
# executions once live trading is separately enabled for an actual trade.
#
# Enforced three independent ways, because a flag that is merely checked before
# submitting gets bypassed by new code paths:
#   1. startup REFUSES if this is combined with BOX_EXECUTION_MODE=live;
#   2. no live adapter is constructed outside live mode, so no object capable of
#      reaching a broker exists;
#   3. a guard turns any attempted submit/modify/cancel into a loud throw.
BOX_SHADOW_MODE_ENABLED=false


# Fallback durable-write delay (ms) paper applies between acquiring a concurrency
# slot and transmitting.
#
# ZERO ON PURPOSE. The live path really does pay two Mongo round trips there,
# inside the already-held slot, before it may send. But until that has actually
# been measured we do not know its size, and a guessed database latency would be
# a fabrication. 0 means "knowingly optimistic on this stage, and it says so" —
# calibrationStatus() reports persistence_window_measured: false. Once
# persistence_wait_ms has samples, paper uses the measured p50 instead. Set this
# only if you have measured your own deployment.
BOX_PAPER_PERSISTENCE_MS=0

# ===========================================================================
# THE FOUR EXECUTION SETTINGS, AND HOW THEY DIFFER
#
# Two independent axes. BOX_EXECUTION_MODE decides whether real orders can exist
# at all; BOX_PAPER_EXECUTION_PROFILE decides how faithfully paper behaves.
#
#   standard     profile. No broker orders. Today's paper behaviour,
#                byte-for-byte: constant latency, no cancel race, no shared
#                liquidity. The comparison baseline.
#
#   live_parity  profile. No broker orders. EVIDENCE-DRIVEN: shared liquidity
#                ledger, the live scheduling policy, and latency + cancel windows
#                drawn from MEASURED live observations when calibration is valid.
#                Every figure reports whether it is measured.
#
#   stress       profile. No broker orders. DELIBERATELY SYNTHETIC fault
#                injection for resilience testing. A separate profile so an
#                injected fault can never be mistaken for observed behaviour.
#                Refuses to start alongside live execution. Never called parity.
#
#   live         MODE. **REAL ORDERS.** The only one of the four that can place
#                them, and only with BOX_LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true as a second
#                gate — without it, startup fails rather than degrading.
#
# WHAT live_parity KNOWS: scheduler wait, durable-persistence latency, transport
# pacing, POST->HTTP response, POST->ACK, ACK->first fill, ACK->terminal,
# partial->terminal and cancel-request->terminal, all measured per broker, per
# operation kind, per marketable/passive profile and per time-of-day bucket.
# Fills come from real observed WebSocket depth walked within a bounded LIMIT.
#
# WHAT live_parity STILL CANNOT KNOW — and therefore never fabricates:
#   * true NSE queue position of our order
#   * hidden or iceberg liquidity
#   * matching-engine ordering
#   * another participant's future order
#   * exact market impact of our own order
#
# THIS IS NOT AN EXACT EXCHANGE SIMULATOR and must never be described as one. It
# is a deterministic digital twin of the OBSERVABLE execution path.
# ===========================================================================

# ===========================================================================
# RECOMMENDED PAPER-VALIDATION CONFIGURATION
#
# Copy this block to validate the simulator against reality. It places NO real
# orders: BOX_EXECUTION_MODE stays paper, and BOX_LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED is
# untouched. The live double gate is deliberately left exactly as it is.
#
#   BOX_EXECUTION_MODE=paper_legging
#   BOX_PAPER_EXECUTION_PROFILE=live_parity
#   BOX_QUEUE_MODEL=haircut
#   BOX_QUEUE_LIQUIDITY_HAIRCUT_PCT=30
#
#   # Scheduler parity: paper must use the SAME cap and pacing as live, or its
#   # queueing model describes a deployment you are not running.
#   BOX_PAPER_MAX_CONCURRENT_EXECUTIONS=1     # = BOX_LIVE_MAX_CONCURRENT_EXECUTIONS
#   BOX_LIVE_BROKER_MIN_INTERVAL_MS=250       # shared by both schedulers
#
#   # Measure, and keep what was measured across restarts. Without persistence,
#   # a restart at 09:30 discards the morning's evidence.
#   BOX_EXECUTION_TIMING_METRICS_ENABLED=true
#   BOX_EXECUTION_EVENT_LOOP_METRICS_ENABLED=true
#   BOX_LIVE_TIMING_PERSIST_ENABLED=true
#   BOX_DEPLOYMENT_REGION=ap-south-1          # a LABEL; samples never cross regions
#
# Expect UNCALIBRATED, measured: no and confidence: LOW on day one. That is
# correct: there is no evidence yet. Watch GET /api/box/execution-diagnostics as
# sample counts accumulate and the status climbs.
#
# To run the real strategy against the real feed while submitting nothing, add
# BOX_SHADOW_MODE_ENABLED=true.
#
# DO NOT set BOX_EXECUTION_MODE=live or BOX_LIVE_TRADING_ENABLED=true as part of
# validation. Enabling live trading is a separate, deliberate decision.
# ===========================================================================

config.name: a directory instead of a file
